overview: The six-page sample supports an anonymous route from the sustainability listing to the complete Stegra announcement, and the article text remains readable without JavaScript. Two concrete priorities affect homepage visitors: active video tiles do not all stop when reduced motion is enabled during a visit, and core story discovery disappears without JavaScript. Investigate homepage media loading alongside those fixes: the first transfer records 49.38 MB with some data unmeasured. Corporate sustainability stories provide context about Google’s activities; they do not establish this publication’s footprint, hosting arrangements or progress against website goals.
nextSteps: Make every active homepage autoplay tile respond when reduced motion is enabled during a visit. Verify this alongside opening the page with the preference already active, and retain working manual Play and Pause controls.

Trace homepage video and image requests, including hidden and offscreen media. Test a bounded preload or on-demand candidate with story discovery and playback intact, then compare the same loading task.
Provide core homepage and sustainability-listing story links in HTML, or a clear lightweight index. Verify an anonymous reader can find and read the featured story without JavaScript.

Inspect the related-story and author-image renditions, narrow navigation, keyboard focus and printed output. Obtain one publication-specific editorial decision and a website impact statement with a dated baseline and goal.

findings.title: Stop autoplay tiles when reduced motion is switched on
findings.summary: Two visible homepage videos continue playing when reduced motion is enabled during the visit. They are paused when the page is opened with that preference already active. Pause controls are present; the defect concerns the preference-change response.
findings.whyItMatters: A visitor who changes the device setting while reading still encounters movement the site already avoids at page opening. Responding consistently would honor that choice throughout the visit.
findings.action: Apply the initial reduced-motion logic to live preference changes. Verify every active visible autoplay tile pauses, then confirm manual Play and Pause remain usable.

findings.title: Investigate video loading before readers choose playback
findings.summary: The first homepage visit records 49.38 MB before notice acknowledgement or scrolling, with some transfer unmeasured. Autoplay and preloaded media are present, including hidden or offscreen media. This loading question is separate from the demonstrated reduced-motion defect.
findings.whyItMatters: Homepage readers incur substantial media transfer before selecting a story or video. Deferring suitable media could be useful, but a safe activation strategy and achievable reduction have not been established.
findings.action: Trace which elements initiate the largest requests. Test a bounded preload or on-demand candidate with thumbnails, story discovery and Play/Pause intact, then compare the same task before estimating any reduction.

findings.title: Serve story-discovery links without JavaScript
findings.summary: With JavaScript disabled, the homepage loses most feed content and the sustainability listing loses its featured and latest-story links. Article reading text remains available once the article URL is reached.
findings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot use the sampled collections to discover those stories when scripts are unavailable. The existing readable articles provide a useful destination for a lightweight discovery route.
findings.action: Render core featured and latest-story links in HTML or add a clear index available without scripts. Verify the listing-to-Stegra reading task with JavaScript disabled.

findings.title: Compare story-card and author-photo renditions
findings.summary: The Stegra article loads a 2784-pixel related-story image at roughly 283 displayed pixels, while some 100-pixel author photos display at 240 pixels. The sample also includes responsive WebP delivery and lazy loading. Necessary detail and quality at intended densities remain unresolved.
findings.whyItMatters: The large card may offer a lighter rendition, while the small headshots may need a sharper one. Pixel counts alone cannot decide the right quality or establish savings.
findings.action: Inspect the cited images at their actual display sizes on standard and high-density screens. Compare alternative renditions, retaining editorial detail and legibility, then measure any transfer change.

checks.title: Check whether moving tiles compete with choosing a story
checks.summary: The captured pages retain headings and recognizable tasks. The homepage has simultaneously playing muted videos and a rotating feature area, with pause controls identified but not exercised. The snapshots do not establish whether movement interrupts the browsing task.
checks.nextStep: Observe a complete homepage story-selection task, activate the pause controls and assess whether moving content competes with reading or navigation.

checks.title: Inspect the cookie notice’s actual choice route
checks.summary: The cookie control says OK, got it and acknowledges a notice. It is not a tested accept/reject pair. Newsletter signup is optional with clear opt-out wording, but visual steering, cookie defaults and a rejection route were not established.
checks.nextStep: Inspect the linked cookie controls and their actual behavior in the represented context. Capture appearance if judging prominence or steering.

checks.title: The sampled English tasks use clear wording
checks.summary: Topic, article, newsletter and about headings identify their purposes. The Stegra announcement names authors and a date and explains its purchasing arrangement; newsletter copy describes weekly updates and opt-out. This reading judgment does not independently verify corporate claims.
checks.nextStep: Keep short task labels and explanations of specialist terms, and validate broader comprehension with the relevant audience.

checks.title: Navigation labels repeat across templates
checks.summary: The six pages keep the same Innovation & AI, Products & platforms, Company news, Feed and Newsletter labels, with consistent search and region controls. Article breadcrumbs and follow/share controls recur. A documented design system was not verified.
checks.nextStep: Keep these shared labels aligned when revising menus, article templates and topic pages.

checks.title: Stop active tiles when reduced motion is enabled
checks.summary: Two visible homepage videos continue playing after reduced motion is enabled during the visit. Opening the page with that preference already active leaves them paused. Named pause controls are present; the demonstrated problem is the response to a preference change.
checks.nextStep: Apply the same preference logic to active videos as to initial page loading. Verify every visible autoplay tile pauses, with manual replay and pause still available.

checks.title: No unsolicited notification request was observed
checks.summary: No notification-permission call appears in the six captured states. Newsletter entry is an explicit choice with opt-out wording, and no unsolicited notification dialog was observed. Permission was already denied and no signup was submitted.
checks.nextStep: Recheck any new notification feature in a fresh undecided-permission context; test subscription behavior separately if it enters scope.

checks.title: Inspect print overflow and relevant downloads
checks.summary: Article and about pages load a print stylesheet and retain their main text in print emulation. The homepage retains horizontal overflow and some templates keep navigation. Download links include repeated PDF references and hidden video fallbacks, but their contents and physical pagination were not inspected.
checks.nextStep: Inspect actual homepage and article print output for overflow and page breaks. Open any task-relevant download before judging its quality or equivalence.

checks.title: Check module use across complete journeys
checks.summary: The brief initial coverage can nominate the common bundle, page chunks and player/carousel code for investigation. It omits complete search, menu, feed expansion, playback and signup tasks, and function samples are truncated. Unexecuted ranges do not establish safely removable code.
checks.nextStep: Record coverage across representative interactions and identify specific modules before deciding what can be removed.

checks.title: Investigate the homepage’s early media loading
checks.summary: The publication already loads separate code chunks. The first homepage transfer records 49.38 MB with some data unmeasured, alongside autoplay and preloaded video. Optional players and widgets are identifiable, but a usable on-demand alternative and exact activation costs were not tested.
checks.nextStep: Trace media initiators and test a bounded preload or on-demand strategy for one expensive optional feature. Compare existing chunks and verify story discovery and playback before proposing further splitting.

checks.title: Inspect homepage overflow and the narrow menu
checks.summary: Five templates retain task text without recorded horizontal overflow. The homepage measures 2368 pixels across in a 1280-pixel viewport, while narrow emulation removes that overflow. Carousel content could account for it; no captured image or control activation establishes a clipped task.
checks.nextStep: Inspect homepage horizontal scrolling and feature controls, then complete the article route through the narrow menu.

checks.title: Test useful alternatives before adding data-use guidance
checks.summary: The Stegra article offers reading and optional audio, the Fitbit article offers a selected video, and some homepage media autoplays. Relative transfer, a working stop-all choice and transcript alternatives were not tested. Industrial steel claims do not describe the impact of reading the publication.
checks.nextStep: Exercise media controls and text alternatives, measure their relative transfer and use that evidence for any contextual data-use guidance.

checks.title: Readers can reach the featured sustainability article
checks.summary: The recorded pointer journey acknowledges the cookie notice, opens the featured Stegra story and reaches its canonical URL, full headline and readable main body without login. The result supports this route’s completion, without proving an optimal journey length.
checks.nextStep: Retain this route in navigation checks and test other audience constraints independently.

checks.title: Inspect large story cards and small author photos
checks.summary: The sample includes responsive WebP cards and lazy loading, alongside large homepage assets and 100-pixel author photos displayed at 240 pixels. A related-story image on the Stegra article is 2784 pixels wide at roughly 283 displayed pixels. Acceptable quality at intended densities was not established.
checks.nextStep: Compare the cited card and author-image renditions at their actual display sizes and intended pixel densities before choosing a smaller or sharper version.

checks.title: Loaded fonts provide fallbacks for the sampled text
checks.summary: Observed Google Sans regular and medium faces serve body and heading text with a swap loading policy and Roboto/Arial/Helvetica fallbacks. Many declared language-range faces are not loaded. Font declarations alone do not establish unnecessary downloads.
checks.nextStep: Retain usable fallbacks and test the required language coverage before removing or changing font files.

checks.title: Task controls have naming relationships
checks.summary: All six pages declare English and have a main region and meaningful task headings. Search, menu, media, region and newsletter controls have names, including the required email field. Multiple feature headings on the homepage do not by themselves fail this bounded check.
checks.nextStep: Keep labels and landmarks when updating templates; assess interactive states and full accessible names in a dedicated accessibility review.

checks.title: Titles and canonical addresses support page discovery
checks.summary: All six pages have task-descriptive titles and matching absolute canonicals. Declared structured data parses, including article and about-page data. The newsletter’s simple title/canonical meets this narrow check; schema validity and search eligibility were not assessed.
checks.nextStep: Keep metadata aligned with the page purpose when stories or topic routes change.

checks.title: Apply reduced motion when the preference changes
checks.summary: Enabling reduced motion during the homepage visit pauses one video but leaves two visible autoplay videos running. Opening with the preference already active leaves them paused. Text remains available; a light palette alone establishes no theme defect.
checks.nextStep: Reuse initial reduced-motion handling for live changes and verify all visible autoplay tiles stop while manual playback remains usable.

checks.title: Make core story links available without JavaScript
checks.summary: The Stegra and Fitbit article text, newsletter explanation and about page remain readable without scripts. The sustainability listing loses its featured and latest story links, and the homepage loses most feed content. No explicit alternative index supports that core discovery task.
checks.nextStep: Serve the core topic and story links in HTML or provide a discoverable lightweight index. Verify a reader can find the featured article without scripts.

checks.title: Trace collection updates before removing requests
checks.summary: The pages make analytics and article-collection requests. The bounded capture does not distinguish every repeat from pagination or necessary updates and provides no backend cost. A completed article visit does not establish the necessity of every background call.
checks.nextStep: Group homepage and topic requests by initiator, parameters and update event, then investigate repeats with no changed content or task need.

checks.title: Reusable publication assets have cache lifetimes
checks.summary: Versioned scripts and styles have long public lifetimes; font styles and external helpers have shorter private lifetimes, and media exposes validators or lifetimes. These headers support a reuse policy. Actual warm-load reuse and offline support were not tested.
checks.nextStep: Retain suitable lifetimes and validators; measure a matched repeat visit before claiming a cache-performance improvement.

checks.title: Material text responses use compression
checks.summary: The sampled successful HTML, scripts, styles and JSON/text responses use gzip or Brotli. No material successful uncompressed text response appears in the six bounded network records. Video, WebP and font files need separate delivery decisions.
checks.nextStep: Keep negotiated text compression enabled and recheck new material text endpoints when adding features.

checks.title: Inspect focus on the initial cookie controls
checks.summary: Initial Tab traces reach meaningful cookie, skip, home and navigation controls. Skip and home have solid blue outlines; cookie outlines are transparent and other possible focus styling was not captured. The cookie controls’ visible focus remains unresolved.
checks.nextStep: Capture the focused cookie link and button, including background, border and shadow changes, then continue through the remaining initial controls.

checks.title: Provide an impact statement for the publication
checks.summary: The sustainability listing and Stegra announcement describe Google products, operations, industrial materials and partnerships. They do not identify resource use or mitigation for blog.google. The bounded search does not prove that a publication-specific statement is absent elsewhere.
checks.nextStep: Provide a public statement naming this publication and explaining its environmental impacts, boundary and mitigation.

checks.title: Publish a useful, verifiable carbon.txt record
checks.summary: The tested root and well-known carbon.txt routes return 404, with no usable header or DNS route to a parsed document. This fails the narrow discovery expectation without establishing high publication emissions or the absence of corporate sustainability work.
checks.nextStep: If useful for evidence discovery, publish a parseable carbon.txt with verified relationships and confirm the advertised route resolves.

checks.title: Connect operational hosting evidence to blog.google
checks.summary: Google Cloud/storage hostnames and corporate energy statements do not by themselves identify this publication’s hosting boundary or independently substantiate its electricity sourcing. That chain of evidence remains unavailable.
checks.nextStep: Link this origin to its hosting service and provide dated, independently corroborated operational evidence before making a hosting sustainability claim.

checks.title: The observed article route needs no account
checks.summary: The anonymous English desktop pointer journey reaches the complete Stegra article after acknowledging the notice, with no personal-data entry or account gate. Keyboard, geography and constrained-device success were outside the task.
checks.nextStep: Retain the anonymous reading route and test those excluded constraints separately before generalizing access findings.

checks.title: The newsletter form asks for an explained email purpose
checks.summary: Before submission, the newsletter asks only for a required email address to deliver weekly news and stories, and states an opt-out choice. No email was entered and no signup, delivery, unsubscribe, retention or deletion behavior was verified. The broad privacy policy does not establish publication-specific processing.
checks.nextStep: Keep the email-only entry and clear purpose. Test delivery, unsubscribe and data handling separately if those later stages enter scope.

checks.title: Show one applied editorial review decision
checks.summary: Article dates, author attribution, the about page and current listing establish a functioning news collection. They do not show a review trigger or schedule and an executed update, archive or deletion decision. Historical announcements may retain reader value.
checks.nextStep: Provide a collection-specific review schedule or trigger and one dated decision with its rationale, keeping historical access where it remains useful.

checks.title: Set a publication-specific goal with comparable progress
checks.summary: The Stegra estimates and construction examples concern corporate materials procurement. Neither they nor the about page provide a resource metric, baseline, target and comparable progress for blog.google. This is an evidence gap for the publication, not a failed corporate target.
checks.nextStep: Provide a publication-specific resource or impact goal, its measurement boundary and a dated baseline and progress record measured on the same basis.
